column1: Deploy MailHog to cluster as a test SMTP server
column26:
Deploy MailHog as an in-cluster SMTP server so the test suite can receive and inspect emails without requiring external SMTP access.

*Background*

The cluster's {{00-default-deny}} network policy blocks all outbound traffic. Port 587 to {{smtp.gmail.com}} has no egress policy, so emails cannot leave the cluster. The current {{test_api.py}} works around this at line 387 by inserting voting tokens directly into the database via {{kubectl exec psql}}, bypassing the email flow entirely. MailHog replaces this workaround by catching emails inside the cluster.

Additionally, {{SMTP_USER}} and {{SMTP_PASS}} are currently missing from {{admin-deployment.yaml}} entirely. This causes Gmail auth to silently fail — {{SMTP_PASS}} defaults to {{""}} in {{shared/email_util.py}}, which short-circuits the credentials check before any connection is attempted.

----

*Deliverable 1 — Create* {{k8s/mailhog/mailhog-deployment.yaml}}

MailHog is a *local development tool only*. This manifest must be scoped to {{uvote-dev}} and must never be promoted to {{uvote-test}} or {{uvote-prod}}.

* Image: {{mailhog/mailhog:latest}}
* SMTP port: {{1025}} (receives emails from services)
* HTTP API port: {{8025}} (used by tests to retrieve emails)
* Namespace: {{uvote-dev}}
* Service type: {{ClusterIP}} (internal only, not exposed via Ingress)

----

*Deliverable 2 — Create network policy:* {{k8s/network-policies/05-allow-mailhog.yaml}}

Create two {{NetworkPolicy}} resources following the established two-policy pattern from {{02-allow-to-database.yaml}} and {{04-allow-audit.yaml}}:

* {{allow-mailhog-egress}} (policy-order: {{05a}}): egress from {{app: admin-service}} to {{mailhog:1025}}, plus DNS
* {{allow-mailhog-ingress}} (policy-order: {{05b}}): ingress to {{app: mailhog}} from {{app: admin-service}} on port {{1025}}

Note: {{voter-service/}} source code is deployed as a Kubernetes Deployment named {{admin-service}} with label {{app: admin-service}}. This is the service that sends voting token emails via {{shared/email_util.py}}.

----

*Deliverable 3 — Update* {{admin-deployment.yaml}} *and* {{deploy_platform.py}}

Per *ADR011*, SMTP credentials must never be stored as inline {{value:}} fields in deployment manifests. They are created at deploy time by {{deploy_platform.py}} using {{kubectl create secret}}, and pods reference them via {{secretKeyRef}}. This is the same pattern used for {{db-credentials}}, {{jwt-secret}}, and {{flask-secret}}.

{{admin-deployment.yaml}} — replace any existing inline SMTP {{value:}} fields with {{secretKeyRef}} entries pointing to an {{smtp-credentials}} Secret:

{noformat}- name: SMTP_HOST
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_HOST
- name: SMTP_PORT
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_PORT
- name: SMTP_USE_TLS
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_USE_TLS
- name: SMTP_FROM
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_FROM
- name: SMTP_USER
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_USER
      optional: true
- name: SMTP_PASS
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: SMTP_PASS
      optional: true
- name: FRONTEND_URL
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: smtp-credentials
      key: FRONTEND_URL
{noformat}

The manifest must remain identical and valid across all environments. No environment-specific values ({{mailhog}}, {{1025}}, etc.) may appear as inline {{value:}} fields.

{{deploy_platform.py}} — add an {{smtp-credentials}} secret creation block in the secrets section, with a prominent comment marking it as dev/local only:

{noformat}# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# SMTP credentials — DEV/LOCAL ONLY (MailHog)
# This secret points to the in-cluster MailHog fake SMTP server.
# MailHog is NOT deployed in uvote-test or uvote-prod.
# For production namespaces, replace these values with real SMTP provider
# credentials before creating this secret.
# admin-deployment.yaml is environment-agnostic — it reads SMTP config
# from this secret via secretKeyRef regardless of environment.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
kubectl create secret generic smtp-credentials \
  --from-literal=SMTP_HOST=mailhog \
  --from-literal=SMTP_PORT=1025 \
  --from-literal=SMTP_USE_TLS=false \
  --from-literal=SMTP_FROM=uvote@test.local \
  --from-literal=SMTP_USER="" \
  --from-literal=SMTP_PASS="" \
  --from-literal=FRONTEND_URL=http://frontend-service:5000 \
  --namespace=uvote-dev \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
{noformat}

----

*Implementation Note — Why* {{secretKeyRef}} *instead of inline values*

The original ticket described setting env vars as inline {{value:}} fields. During implementation this was revised to use {{secretKeyRef}} in order to comply with ADR011 and keep {{admin-deployment.yaml}} environment-agnostic. Inline MailHog values in the base manifest would be inherited by {{uvote-test}} and {{uvote-prod}} on promotion, pointing those environments at a service that does not exist outside {{uvote-dev}}. The {{secretKeyRef}} pattern isolates all environment-specific SMTP configuration to {{deploy_platform.py}}, which is the established and approved approach for all credentials in this project.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

* {{k8s/mailhog/mailhog-deployment.yaml}} exists, deploys to {{uvote-dev}} only, exposes ports {{1025}} and {{8025}}
* {{05-allow-mailhog.yaml}} permits egress from {{admin-service}} to {{mailhog:1025}} and ingress to {{mailhog}} from {{admin-service}}
* {{admin-deployment.yaml}} contains zero inline {{value:}} fields for SMTP configuration — all SMTP env vars use {{secretKeyRef}} pointing to {{smtp-credentials}}
* {{deploy_platform.py}} creates the {{smtp-credentials}} secret with MailHog values for {{uvote-dev}}, with a comment clearly marking it as dev-only
* No MailHog references appear in {{shared/email_util.py}} or any production application code

column1: Write test helper function to query MailHog API and extract voting token URL
column26:
Write a helper function that queries the MailHog HTTP API to retrieve the
voting token URL sent by voter-service after token generation.

The voter-service sends voting token emails via send_voting_token_email() in
shared/email_util.py. The email contains a direct voting URL in the format:
  {FRONTEND_URL}/vote/{token}

There is no OTP code to extract — the token IS the credential. The test helper
needs to parse the URL from the email body.

Note: send_otp_email() in shared/email_util.py is completely unused dead code —
it is never called from any service. Do not reference it in tests.

Implement in tests/helpers/mailhog.py:

  import httpx

  MAILHOG_API = "[http://localhost:8025/api/v2/messages|http://localhost:8025/api/v2/messages]"

  async def get_latest_voting_token(voter_email: str) -> str:
      """Query MailHog API, find email to voter_email, extract /vote/{token} URL."""
      response = await httpx.AsyncClient().get(MAILHOG_API)
      messages = response.json()["items"]
      for msg in messages:
          recipients = [r["Mailbox"] + "@" + r["Domain"]
                        for r in msg["To"]]
          if voter_email in recipients:
              body = msg["Content"]["Body"]
              # Extract token from URL: /vote/{token}
              token = body.split("/vote/")[1].split('"')[0].strip()
              return token
      raise AssertionError(f"No email found for {voter_email} in MailHog")

The shared/ directory contains 3 modules that every service depends on,
none of which have any tests:

  shared/security.py
  shared/schemas.py
  shared/database.py

Create tests/test_shared.py covering:

  security.py:

* Token generation: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) produces a 43-character
URL-safe string — assert length and character set
* BALLOT_TOKEN_SECRET: assert that the hardcoded fallback default is
not used when the env var is set (this is the security risk flagged
in the audit at shared/security.py lines 64-66)
* bcrypt password hashing: assert hash is produced and verify() returns
True for correct password, False for wrong password
* JWT encoding/decoding: assert payload round-trips correctly with
organiser_id, email, exp fields intact

  schemas.py:

* Pydantic model validation: assert that required fields raise
ValidationError when missing
* EmailStr fields: assert invalid email formats are rejected
* Assert that TokenVerifyResponse only exposes {valid, organiser_id,
email, error} — election_id and voter_id are intentionally stripped
from the HTTP response (noted in test_api.py Check 4 comments)

  database.py:

* Connection pool initialisation: mock asyncpg.create_pool and assert
it is called with the correct DATABASE_URL env var
* Assert pool is singleton — calling init_db() twice does not create
a second pool
* Assert get_db() raises a meaningful error if pool is not initialised

Add to requirements-dev.txt if not already present:
  pytest-asyncio==0.23.0  (required for async pool tests)
  pytest-mock==3.12.0     (required for mocking asyncpg and env vars)

column1: Reconcile database schema and separate concerns into three files
column26:
The project currently has two divergent SQL schema files that are causing runtime failures across all application services:

{{uvote-platform/k8s/database/schema.sql}} (Luke) — simple schema used by the Kubernetes cluster. Contains {{admins}}, {{elections}}, {{candidates}}, {{voters}}, {{voting_tokens}}, {{votes}}, {{audit_logs}}. Also contains {{CREATE USER}}, {{GRANT}}, and {{INSERT}} seed data mixed into the same file.

{{database/init.sql}} (Hafsa) — full production schema used by Docker Compose. Contains {{organisations}}, {{organisers}}, {{elections}}, {{voters}}, {{voter_mfa}}, {{election_options}}, {{voting_tokens}}, {{blind_tokens}}, {{encrypted_ballots}}, {{vote_receipts}}, {{tallied_votes}}. Has pgcrypto, anonymity bridge design, and automatic hash triggers. Missing: {{audit_log}} table, database roles, and GRANTs.

All application services were written against {{init.sql}}. The Kubernetes cluster runs {{schema.sql}}. This mismatch causes {{UndefinedTableError}} at runtime — for example {{auth-service}} crashes with {{relation "organisers" does not exist}} because the cluster is missing the correct tables.

----

*Root Cause*

The two schemas were developed independently without coordination. The cluster schema and the application code are pointing at different table names throughout.

----

*Deliverables*

Produce three new files that replace {{schema.sql}} on the cluster. {{database/init.sql}} must not be modified.

*File 1 —* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/schema.sql}} *(replace existing)*

Combined schema containing table definitions, indexes, triggers, and extensions only. No {{CREATE USER}}, no {{GRANT}}, no {{INSERT}}.

* Base: {{init.sql}} — use as-is, it is the correct application schema
* Add: {{audit_log}} table following the {{init.sql}} design pattern ({{event_type}}, {{actor_type}}, {{actor_id}}, {{detail JSONB}}, {{event_hash}}, {{previous_hash}})
* Add: immutability trigger on {{audit_log}} matching the {{encrypted_ballots}} pattern ({{prevent_audit_modification}}, {{immutable_audit}})
* Add: auto-hash trigger on {{audit_log}} matching the {{generate_ballot_hash}} pattern ({{generate_audit_hash}}, {{auto_audit_hash}})
* Keep: {{DROP TABLE IF EXISTS}} block at top covering all tables in dependency order
* Keep: {{CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;}} after the DROP block
* Add header comment documenting: anonymity vs accountability design principle, table groups (tenancy, identity, election, ballot auth, ledger, audit), and that roles and seed data are in separate files

*File 2 —* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/create_roles.sql}} *(new file)*

All {{CREATE USER}} and {{GRANT}} statements only. No table definitions, no seed data. Applied after {{schema.sql}}.

Take the role definitions from {{schema.sql}} and update all table and sequence names to match the combined schema:

||Role||Access||
|{{auth_service}}|{{organisers}} (not {{admins}})|
|{{voting_service}}|{{encrypted_ballots}} (not {{votes}}), {{election_options}} (not {{candidates}}), {{blind_tokens}}|
|{{election_service}}|{{elections}}, {{election_options}} (not {{candidates}})|
|{{results_service}}|{{encrypted_ballots}}, {{elections}}, {{election_options}}, {{tallied_votes}}|
|{{audit_service}}|{{audit_log}} (not {{audit_logs}})|
|{{admin_service}}|{{voters}}, {{election_options}}, {{voting_tokens}}, {{organisations}}, {{organisers}}|

Add header comment explaining: per-service least-privilege grants, placeholder passwords overridden at deploy time by {{deploy_platform.py}}, apply order.

*File 3 —* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/seed_data.sql}} *(new file)*

All {{INSERT}} statements only. No table definitions, no roles. Applied after {{create_roles.sql}}.

* {{INSERT INTO organisations}} — Demo University
* {{INSERT INTO organisers}} — {{admin@uvote.com}} / bcrypt hash of {{admin123}}, {{org_id = 1}}
* {{INSERT INTO elections}} — Student Council 2026, {{organiser_id = 1}}
* {{INSERT INTO election_options}} (not {{candidates}}) — Alice Johnson, Bob Smith, Carol White, {{election_id = 1}}

All table names must match the combined schema. Add header comment warning that this is development/test seed data only and the admin password must be changed before any real deployment.

----

*Apply order*

{noformat}schema.sql → create_roles.sql → seed_data.sql
{noformat}

{{deploy_platform.py}} must be updated to apply all three files in this order. This is a follow-up task within this ticket.

----

*Constraints*

* Do not modify {{database/init.sql}}
* Do not modify any application service code
* {{schema.sql}} must contain zero {{CREATE USER}}, {{GRANT}}, or {{INSERT}} statements
* {{create_roles.sql}} must contain zero {{CREATE TABLE}} statements
* {{seed_data.sql}} must contain zero {{CREATE TABLE}} statements
* All three files must be valid PostgreSQL
* If {{init.sql}} already contains an {{audit_log}} table use it as-is — do not create a duplicate

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/schema.sql}} contains only table definitions, indexes, triggers, and extensions
* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/create_roles.sql}} exists and contains all role creation and grant statements with correct table names
* {{uvote-platform/k8s/database/seed_data.sql}} exists and contains all seed data with correct table names
* {{deploy_platform.py}} applies all three files in order during cluster setup
* Running {{setup_k8s_platform.py}} followed by {{deploy_platform.py}} produces a cluster where {{auth-service}} starts without {{UndefinedTableError}}
* {{test_db.py --quick}} passes all 10 tests against the rebuilt cluster

column1: Add unit tests for shared/logging_config.py
column26:
Create a pytest unit test file at {{tests/test_logging_config.py}} that validates the centralised logging configuration introduced in {{shared/logging_config.py}}. The tests must run without a live database or running services — no cluster, no Docker, no external dependencies.

----

*Test Cases*

*1 —* {{configure_logging()}} *installs a handler on the root logger*

Call {{configure_logging()}} and assert that {{logging.getLogger('')}} has at least one handler attached. This confirms {{dictConfig}} applied successfully.

*2 — Output is valid JSON*

After calling {{configure_logging()}}, redirect the root logger's stream handler to a {{io.StringIO}} buffer, emit one {{logger.info(...)}} call, and assert the captured line parses with {{json.loads()}} without raising an exception.

*3 — Required fields are present in every log line*

Parse the captured JSON and assert all four fields are present: {{asctime}}, {{name}}, {{levelname}}, {{message}}.

*4 —* {{asctime}} *matches the configured date format*

Assert the {{asctime}} value matches the pattern {{%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ}} (e.g. {{2026-03-20T14:00:00Z}}). Use {{datetime.strptime()}} to validate — do not use regex.

*5 — Logger name is preserved correctly*

Call {{logging.getLogger('auth-service')}} after {{configure_logging()}}, emit a log line, and assert the {{name}} field in the JSON output equals {{"auth-service"}}. Repeat for one other service name (e.g. {{"voter-service"}}).

*6 — Log level is reflected in output*

Emit one {{logger.info(...)}} and one {{logger.warning(...)}} call, capture both lines, and assert {{levelname}} is {{"INFO"}} and {{"WARNING"}} respectively.

*7 — Messages below INFO are suppressed*

Emit a {{logger.debug(...)}} call and assert nothing is written to the buffer (i.e. the root logger level of {{INFO}} is enforced).

*8 —* {{configure_logging()}} *is idempotent*

Call {{configure_logging()}} twice and assert the root logger does not accumulate duplicate handlers (i.e. {{len(logging.getLogger('').handlers)}} does not increase on the second call). If the current implementation does not handle this, the test should document the behaviour and be marked {{xfail}} until fixed.

----

*Implementation Notes*

* Use {{pytest}} with {{io.StringIO}} to capture log output — do not write to disk or use {{capfd}}.
* Add a {{@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)}} that resets {{logging.root.handlers}} to {{[]}} before each test to prevent state leakage between cases (mirrors the function-scoped rollback pattern used in {{test_api.py}}).
* {{pythonjsonlogger}} must be installed in the test environment. Add it to a {{requirements-test.txt}} or the existing {{requirements.txt}} in {{shared/}} if not already present.
* Run with: {{python3 -m pytest tests/test_logging_config.py -v}}

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

* [ ] All 8 test cases implemented in {{tests/test_logging_config.py}}
* [ ] All tests pass with {{pytest}} and produce no warnings
* [ ] No running cluster, database, or service is required to execute the suite
* [ ] Tests are isolated — passing or failing one does not affect another

column1: Add health check assertions for all services to test_api.py
Fix setup_k8s_platform.py to apply create_roles.sql and seed_data.sql
column26:
setup_k8s_platform.py apply_database_schema() (line 323) applies only
schema.sql. The two additional SQL files at the same path are never applied:

  uvote-platform/k8s/database/create_roles.sql
  uvote-platform/k8s/database/seed_data.sql

Current code:
  schema_file = k8s_dir / "database" / "schema.sql"

h1. only this file is piped to psql — nothing else

Impact:

* seed_data.sql not applied → no default organiser account ([admin@uvote.com|mailto:admin@uvote.com]),
no sample election, no election options → system is unrunnable after fresh
cluster setup. BREAKING.
* create_roles.sql not applied → six per-service PostgreSQL users
(auth_service, voting_service, election_service, results_service,
audit_service, admin_service) and their GRANT statements are never
created. All services currently fall back to uvote_admin superuser.

Fix: After applying schema.sql, apply create_roles.sql then seed_data.sql
in the correct order using the same kubectl exec psql pattern already
in the function:

h1. Step 1 — already done

  kubectl exec postgresql -- psql -U uvote_admin -d uvote < schema.sql

h1. Step 2 — add this

  kubectl exec postgresql -- psql -U uvote_admin -d uvote < create_roles.sql

h1. Step 3 — add this

  kubectl exec postgresql -- psql -U uvote_admin -d uvote < seed_data.sql

Order is critical — create_roles.sql depends on tables existing (schema.sql
must be applied first), and seed_data.sql depends on roles existing
(create_roles.sql must be applied second).

column1: Expose /metrics endpoint on all FastAPI services
column26:
Wire prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator into all 6 FastAPI app.py files
to expose a /metrics endpoint on each service.

Add the following to each app.py after app initialisation:

  from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator
  Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)

This automatically instruments all existing routes and exposes:

* http_requests_total (counter by method, path, status)
* http_request_duration_seconds (histogram — p50/p95/p99 latency)
* http_requests_in_progress (gauge)

Services and their ports for Prometheus scrape config:
  auth-service:     5001/metrics
  election-service: 5002/metrics
  voting-service:   5003/metrics
  results-service:  5004/metrics
  voter-service:    5002/metrics (deployed as admin-service)
  frontend-service: 5000/metrics

The platform infrastructure doc identifies these SLIs as targets:

* Request rate per service per endpoint
* Response time percentiles (p50, p95, p99)
* Error rate per service (5xx_responses / total_responses * 100)
* Active DB connections per pool

Note: the zero-trust network policies (00-default-deny) will block
Prometheus from scraping /metrics unless an egress policy is added
allowing Prometheus pod → each service on the service port.
Create k8s/network-policies/05-allow-prometheus-scrape.yaml as part
of this ticket.

No service currently exposes a /metrics endpoint. The platform infrastructure

column1: Deploy Prometheus to local Kind cluster
column26:
Deploy Prometheus to the uvote-dev namespace on the local Kind cluster
using the kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart.

The platform infrastructure doc confirms Prometheus is fully absent —
grep for "prometheus" in k8s/ returns 0 YAML matches, only ADR references.

Install via Helm:
  helm repo add prometheus-community \
    [https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts|https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts|smart-link] 
  helm install prometheus prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack \
    --namespace monitoring --create-namespace \
    -f k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml

Create k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml with scrape config
targeting all 6 UVote services:

  additionalScrapeConfigs:
    - job_name: uvote-services
      static_configs:
        - targets:
          - auth-service.uvote-dev:5001
          - election-service.uvote-dev:5002
          - voting-service.uvote-dev:5003
          - results-service.uvote-dev:5004
          - admin-service.uvote-dev:5002
          - frontend-service.uvote-dev:5000
      metrics_path: /metrics
      scrape_interval: 15s

Verify Prometheus is scraping all 6 services by checking
Prometheus UI → Status → Targets — all should show State: UP.

Key security metrics to monitor per the network security doc:

* Failed admin login attempts > 10/min → P1 alert
* NetworkPolicy deny count > 100/min sustained → P1 alert
* Pod restart count > 3 in 5 minutes → P2 alert
* DB connection count > 80% of max_connections → P2 alert

column1: Deploy Grafana to local Kind cluster and configure Prometheus datasource
column26:
Deploy Grafana to the monitoring namespace on the local Kind cluster.
Grafana is included in the kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart installed
in the previous ticket — enable it via prometheus-values.yaml:

  grafana:
    enabled: true
    adminPassword: "uvote-grafana-admin"
    service:
      type: ClusterIP

Configure Prometheus as the default datasource:
  grafana:
    datasources:
      datasources.yaml:
        apiVersion: 1
        datasources:
          - name: Prometheus
            type: prometheus
            url: [http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus:9090|http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus:9090]
            isDefault: true

Verify by port-forwarding Grafana:
  kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/prometheus-grafana 3001:80

Login with admin / uvote-grafana-admin and confirm Prometheus
datasource shows green / "Data source is working".

The platform infrastructure doc planned architecture is:
  Application Pods → /metrics endpoint
  → Prometheus (scrapes every 15s)
  → Grafana (dashboards + alerting)

column1: Create Grafana SLI dashboard for UVote services
column26:
Create a Grafana dashboard covering the SLIs defined in the platform
infrastructure doc for all 6 UVote services.

Create k8s/monitoring/dashboards/uvote-sli-dashboard.json with panels for:

# Request Rate (req/s per service)
PromQL: rate(http_requests_total{job="uvote-services"}[1m])
# Error Rate (5xx responses as % of total)
PromQL: rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[1m])
        / rate(http_requests_total[1m]) * 100
SLO target: < 1% error rate
# Latency p50 / p95 / p99
PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95,
        rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))
SLO target: p95 < 500ms
# Pod Availability (pods running vs desired)
PromQL: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available
        / kube_deployment_spec_replicas
# Active DB Connections per service
PromQL: asyncpg_pool_size (requires custom metric)
# Vote submission rate
PromQL: rate(http_requests_total{path="/vote/submit"}[1m])
# Auth failure rate (failed logins)
PromQL: rate(http_requests_total
        {path="/login", status="401"}[1m])
Alert threshold: > 10/min per the network security doc (P1)

column1: Configure AlertManager rules for UVote
column26:
Create AlertManager alerting rules based on the thresholds defined in
the platform infrastructure and network security docs.

Create k8s/monitoring/alerting-rules.yaml with the following alerts:

  P0 — Critical (hash chain integrity):
    - Hash chain verification failures: any failure triggers immediately
      (no votes should ever fail hash verification)

  P1 — High (active threat indicators):
    - Error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes
    - Failed admin login attempts > 10/min
    - NetworkPolicy deny count > 100/min sustained
    - Ingress request rate > 1000 req/s sustained

  P2 — Warning (resource pressure):
    - Pod restart count > 3 in 5 minutes
    - DB connection count > 80% of max_connections
    - Any pod in CrashLoopBackOff state
    - Certificate expiry < 7 days (future)

Configure AlertManager to route P0/P1 alerts to a Slack webhook
or email. For local Kind cluster, log to alertmanager stdout is
acceptable for demo purposes.

Add to prometheus-values.yaml:
  alertmanager:
    enabled: true
    config:
      route:
        receiver: uvote-alerts
      receivers:
        - name: uvote-alerts

column1: Deploy Elasticsearch single-node to local Kind cluster
column26:
Deploy a single-node Elasticsearch instance to the monitoring namespace
on the local Kind cluster.

The platform infrastructure doc confirms Elasticsearch is completely absent —
grep -r elasticsearch . returns 0 matches in code or manifests.

Deploy using the Elastic Helm chart:
  helm repo add elastic [https://helm.elastic.co|https://helm.elastic.co]
  helm install elasticsearch elastic/elasticsearch \
    --namespace monitoring \
    -f k8s/logging/elasticsearch-values.yaml

Create k8s/logging/elasticsearch-values.yaml for single-node Kind setup:
  replicas: 1
  minimumMasterNodes: 1
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi
    limits:
      cpu: 1000m
      memory: 2Gi
  volumeClaimTemplate:
    resources:
      requests:
        storage: 5Gi

Note: default Elasticsearch requests 2Gi RAM per node. The Kind cluster
runs on approximately 16GB RAM shared with all 6 UVote services.
Limit Elasticsearch to 2Gi to avoid starving the application pods.

Verify by port-forwarding:
  kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/elasticsearch-master 9200:9200
  curl [http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health|http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health]

Expected: {"status":"green"} or {"status":"yellow"} for single-node.

column1: Deploy Fluent Bit as DaemonSet for container log collection
column26:
Deploy Fluent Bit as a DaemonSet to collect container logs from all
UVote pods and forward them to Elasticsearch.

Fluent Bit is chosen over Fluentd for lower resource overhead, which
matters on the Kind cluster where RAM is shared with 6 application services.

Deploy using the Fluent Bit Helm chart:
  helm repo add fluent [https://fluent.github.io/helm-charts|https://fluent.github.io/helm-charts|smart-link] 
  helm install fluent-bit fluent/fluent-bit \
    --namespace monitoring \
    -f k8s/logging/fluent-bit-values.yaml

Create k8s/logging/fluent-bit-values.yaml:
  config:
    inputs: |
      [INPUT]
          Name tail
          Path /var/log/containers/uvote-_.log_
          _Parser json_
          _Tag uvote._
          Mem_Buf_Limit 5MB

{noformat}outputs: |
  [OUTPUT]
      Name es
      Match uvote.*
      Host elasticsearch-master.monitoring
      Port 9200
      Index uvote-logs
      Type _doc

filters: |
  [FILTER]
      Name kubernetes
      Match uvote.*
      Merge_Log On
      Keep_Log Off
      K8S-Logging.Parser On{noformat}

This configuration:

* Tails only uvote-* container logs (not system/monitoring pods)
* Parses JSON log output (requires structured logging tickets done first)
* Tags logs with uvote.* for routing to Elasticsearch
* Enriches logs with Kubernetes metadata (pod name, namespace, service)
* Indexes into uvote-logs in Elasticsearch

Note: The structured JSON logging tickets must be completed first.
Without JSON formatting in app.py files, Fluent Bit will ingest
unstructured text that Kibana cannot parse or filter meaningfully.

column1: Deploy Kibana and create uvote-* index pattern
column26:
Deploy Kibana to the monitoring namespace and configure it to index
UVote logs from Elasticsearch.

Deploy using the Elastic Helm chart:
  helm install kibana elastic/kibana \
    --namespace monitoring \
    -f k8s/logging/kibana-values.yaml

Create k8s/logging/kibana-values.yaml:
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi
    limits:
      cpu: 1000m
      memory: 2Gi
  elasticsearchHosts: "[http://elasticsearch-master:9200|http://elasticsearch-master:9200]"

Verify by port-forwarding:
  kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/kibana-kibana 5601:5601

Create the uvote-* index pattern in Kibana:
  Stack Management → Index Patterns → Create index pattern
  Pattern: uvote-logs-*
  Timestamp field: @timestamp

Useful fields available in the index once structured JSON logging
is in place:

* service (auth, election, voting, results, voter, frontend)
* level (INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
* message
* kubernetes.pod_name
* kubernetes.namespace_name

column1: Create Kibana dashboard for UVote log analysis
column26:
Create a Kibana dashboard to surface the most operationally useful log data
from the uvote-logs-* index.

Create the following visualisations and combine into a single dashboard:

# Error log volume over time (line chart)
Filter: level:ERROR
Group by: service
Shows which service is generating the most errors over time
# Auth failure rate (bar chart)
Filter: service:auth AND message:_invalid_ OR message:_failed_
Shows failed login attempts — alert threshold is 10/min per
the network security doc (P1 indicator)
# Vote submission rate (line chart)
Filter: service:voting AND message:_vote_
Shows voting activity during an active election
# SMTP / email failure log entries (table)
Filter: service:voter AND level:ERROR
voter-service is the only service that currently logs email
failures (logger.error on SMTP failure in generate_tokens()).
This table surfaces those failures in Kibana.
# Top error messages (pie chart)
Filter: level:ERROR
Group by: message.keyword
Identifies the most frequent error types across all services
# Log stream by service (table, live tail)
All services, sorted by @timestamp descending
Useful for real-time monitoring during demos
# Audit chain verification results (table) ← new panel
Filter: service:audit
Fields: @timestamp, chain_valid, total_entries, first_broken_id
Shows the full history of every chain verification run from the
audit-service monitor_chain() background task. Each entry is a
structured JSON log emitted every 60 seconds by audit-service.
A chain_valid:false entry in this table means tampering was
detected and should immediately trigger investigation.
Complements the Grafana live stat panel (uvote_audit_chain_valid)
by providing a historical searchable record rather than just
the current state.

Note: panels 1-6 depend on the structured JSON formatter ticket being
completed first. Without JSON formatting in app.py files, Fluent Bit
will ingest unstructured text that Kibana cannot parse or filter.
Panel 7 specifically depends on the audit-service JSON logging additions
in the structured formatter ticket.

column1: Verify hash chain triggers are applied in the live database schema
column26:
The Stage 1 feedback explicitly flagged that hash chaining was documented
but not implemented in the running system.

ADR-007 defines two PostgreSQL trigger functions that should exist in
uvote-platform/k8s/database/schema.sql:

# generate_audit_hash() — fires on INSERT into audit_log, computes:
  SHA256(event_type || election_id || actor_id || created_at || uuid)
  stored in event_hash column
# prevent_audit_modification() — fires BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE on
audit_log, raises exception:
  'Audit log entries are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted'
# generate_vote_hash_trigger — fires on INSERT into votes, populates
vote_hash and previous_hash columns (ballot hash chain)

Verify these triggers exist and are firing in the live cluster:

  kubectl exec -n uvote-dev deployment/postgresql -- psql \
    -U uvote_admin -d uvote -c \
    "SELECT trigger_name, event_manipulation, event_object_table
     FROM information_schema.triggers
     WHERE trigger_schema = 'public';"

Expected triggers:

* generate_audit_hash on INSERT on audit_log
* immutable_audit on UPDATE/DELETE on audit_log
* generate_vote_hash on INSERT on votes
* prevent_vote_update on UPDATE on votes
* prevent_vote_delete on DELETE on votes

If any are missing, the schema.sql has not been fully applied.
Re-apply via setup_k8s_platform.py or manually via kubectl exec psql.

This ticket is a prerequisite for all other hash chain tickets.

column1: Implement audit event logging in all backend services
column26:
The hash chain trigger fires on every INSERT into audit_log, but the
services are not confirmed to be sending audit events consistently.

ADR-007 defines these events that must be logged:

* ADMIN_LOGIN_SUCCESS / ADMIN_LOGIN_FAILURE (auth-service)
* ELECTION_CREATED / ELECTION_OPENED / ELECTION_CLOSED (election-service)
* VOTER_ADDED / TOKEN_GENERATED (voter-service)
* BALLOT_ISSUED (auth-service — blind ballot token)
* VOTE_CAST — must record receipt_token but NEVER candidate_id
(anonymity requirement per ADR-015)
* RESULTS_ACCESSED (results-service)

For each service, audit events must be sent to audit-service:8005
via HTTP POST. The network policy 04-allow-audit.yaml already permits
this traffic from all 6 backend services.

Audit event payload:
  {
    "event_type": "VOTE_CAST",
    "election_id": 42,
    "actor_id": null,       ← null for voter events (anonymity)
    "detail": {
      "receipt_token": "abc123"   ← never include candidate_id
    }
  }

column1: Implement hash chain verification endpoint in audit-service
column26:
The hash chain exists in the database but there is no endpoint to
verify its integrity. Your lecturer needs to see the chain being
actively verified, not just stored.

Add a GET /audit/verify endpoint to audit-service/app.py:

  @app.get("/audit/verify")
  async def verify_chain():
      """
      Reads all audit_log entries in order and recomputes each hash.
      Returns chain_valid: true if unbroken, false + first_broken_id
      if tampering is detected.
      """

The verification logic in Python using hashlib:

  import hashlib

  async def verify_audit_chain(conn):
      rows = await conn.fetch(
          "SELECT log_id, event_type, election_id, actor_id,
                  created_at, event_hash, previous_hash
           FROM audit_log ORDER BY log_id ASC"
      )
      previous_hash = ""
      for row in rows:
          expected = hashlib.sha256(
              (row["event_type"] +
               str(row["election_id"] or "") +
               str(row["actor_id"] or "") +
               str(row["created_at"]) +
               row["previous_hash"]).encode()
          ).hexdigest()
          if row["event_hash"] != expected:
              return {"chain_valid": False,
                      "first_broken_id": row["log_id"]}
          previous_hash = row["event_hash"]
      return {"chain_valid": True, "total_entries": len(rows)}

Note: the exact hash input must match the PostgreSQL trigger in
schema.sql (generate_audit_hash function). Align the Python
computation with the SQL digest() inputs precisely.

This endpoint is internal-only — audit-service has no ingress route
(04-allow-audit.yaml only permits traffic from backend services,
not from the ingress controller). Expose it via kubectl port-forward
for demo purposes.

column1: Fix missing server-side validation on election HTML form endpoint
column26:
POST /elections/create (HTML form endpoint in election-service/app.py) has
no server-side validation on the title field. The JSON API endpoint
POST /elections enforces min_length=1 via Pydantic's ElectionCreate schema,
but the form endpoint bypasses this entirely.

Submitting the form without a title hits a NOT NULL constraint violation on
elections.title and crashes as an unhandled 500 — there is no try/except and
no flash error message to the user.

Discovered and documented in:
  election-service/tests/test_election.py::test_create_election_form_missing_title

----

STEPS TO REPRODUCE:

# Start the platform: python3 plat_scripts/deploy_platform.py
# Log in to the election management UI
# Submit the election creation form with the title field left blank
# Observe: HTTP 500 instead of a user-friendly validation error

----

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR:

* Form re-renders with flash error: "Election title is required"
* Returns HTTP 200
* No DB insert attempted

ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR:

* Form submission reaches DB INSERT with title = "" or title = None
* NOT NULL constraint violation on elections.title
* Propagates as unhandled HTTP 500

----

FIX:

Add server-side validation to the HTML form endpoint in
election-service/app.py before the DB insert:

  if not title or not title.strip():
      flash(request, "Election title is required", "error")
      return templates.TemplateResponse("create_election.html", {
          "request": request
      })

Also validate that at least 2 options are provided, consistent with
the ElectionCreate schema's min_length=2 constraint:

  if not options or len([o for o in options if o.strip()]) < 2:
      flash(request, "At least 2 election options are required", "error")
      return templates.TemplateResponse("create_election.html", {
          "request": request
      })

----

CONSTRAINTS:

* The JSON endpoint POST /elections behaviour must remain unchanged
* Do not modify the ElectionCreate Pydantic schema
* Validation must occur before any DB insert attempt

----

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

* Submitting the form without a title returns HTTP 200 with flash error
"Election title is required"
* Submitting with fewer than 2 options returns HTTP 200 with flash error
"At least 2 election options are required"
* test_create_election_form_missing_title passes and asserts the flash
error rather than documenting a known failure
* POST /elections JSON endpoint behaviour is unchanged

column1: Remove __init__.py from all service test directories to fix combined pytest invocation
column26:
All five service test directories currently have an *init*.py file. This
turns each tests/ directory into a Python package named tests, causing pytest
to register all five conftest.py files under the same module name tests.conftest.
The second registration raises:

  ValueError: Plugin already registered under a different name:
    voting-service/tests/conftest.py
    = <module 'tests.conftest' from 'auth-service/tests/conftest.py'>

This means the full test suite cannot be run in a single invocation. Each
suite must currently be run separately.

Removing *init*.py from the service test directories makes pytest treat
each directory as rootdir-relative rather than as a Python package. Each
conftest.py gets a unique plugin identity based on its filesystem path and
the collision disappears.

  voting-service/tests/*init*.py
  election-service/tests/*init*.py
  frontend-service/tests/*init*.py
  admin-service/tests/*init*.py

tests/conftest.py) does NOT have an *init*.py and must not be touched

column1: Fix Prometheus registry collision crashing combined pytest run after CV-20/21
column26:
CV-20/21 (Prometheus metrics) introduced a regression in the combined test
suite run. prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator registers http_requests_total
and related metrics into the global prometheus_client.REGISTRY at TestClient
startup. When multiple service test suites run in the same pytest process,
the second service to initialise its TestClient crashes with:

  ValueError: Duplicated timeseries in CollectorRegistry:
  {'http_requests', 'http_requests_created', 'http_requests_total'}

This only manifests in the combined run — individual suites pass because
only one service's app is loaded per process.

----

AFFECTED FILES:

  auth-service/tests/conftest.py
  voting-service/tests/conftest.py
  election-service/tests/conftest.py
  frontend-service/tests/conftest.py
  admin-service/tests/conftest.py
  results-service/tests/conftest.py  ← verify uses same importlib pattern

----

THE FIX:

In each conftest, the importlib module loading block currently looks like:

  if _SERVICE_MODULE_NAME not in sys.modules:
      _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
                  _SERVICE_MODULE_NAME, _APP_PATH)
      _module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
      sys.modules[_SERVICE_MODULE_NAME] = _module
      with patch.object(os.path, "isdir", return_value=True):
          _spec.loader.exec_module(_module)

Wrap the exec_module call with an additional patch that replaces
prometheus_client.REGISTRY with a fresh CollectorRegistry() for
each service:

  import prometheus_client
  from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry

  if _SERVICE_MODULE_NAME not in sys.modules:
      _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
                  _SERVICE_MODULE_NAME, _APP_PATH)
      _module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
      sys.modules[_SERVICE_MODULE_NAME] = _module
      _fresh_registry = CollectorRegistry()
      with patch.object(os.path, "isdir", return_value=True), \
           patch.object(prometheus_client, "REGISTRY", _fresh_registry):
          _spec.loader.exec_module(_module)

This gives each service its own isolated Prometheus registry so duplicate
metric name registration never occurs regardless of load order.

----

CONSTRAINTS:

* Add prometheus_client and CollectorRegistry imports at the top of each
conftest if not already present
* Make NO other changes to any conftest file
* Do not touch any app.py files
* Do not modify any test files — conftest files only

----

VERIFICATION:

  After all fixes are applied, run the combined invocation:

{noformat}python -m pytest \\
  auth-service/tests/ \\
  voting-service/tests/ \\
  election-service/tests/ \\
  frontend-service/tests/ \\

* 121 tests pass, 0 errors, 0 failed

* No app.py or test files modified — conftest files only

column1: Add boot orchestrator scripts and fix log file placement
column26:
Deployment scripts currently write log files to the project root, cluttering
the repository. Developers also have no single command to bring up the full
platform from scratch — they must run setup_k8s_platform.py, deploy_platform.py,
and ELK deployment commands separately in the correct order.

----

TASK 1 — Fix log file placement:

All deployment scripts currently write log files to the project root.
Move all log output to a logs/ directory at the project root.

* Create logs/.gitkeep so the directory is tracked in git
* Add logs/*.log to .gitignore
* Update deploy_platform.py:
  log_file = project_root / f"deploy-{timestamp}.log"
  → logs_dir = project_root / "logs"
     logs_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
     log_file = logs_dir / f"deploy-{timestamp}.log"
* Update deploy_test_platform.py with the same pattern:
  log_file = logs_dir / f"deploy-mailhog-{timestamp}.log"
* Each script must create logs/ itself if it does not exist —
do not assume it is present

----

TASK 2 — Create boot_platform.py (dev/production orchestrator):

Create boot_platform.py at the project root. Single command to go from
nothing to a fully running platform. Calls existing scripts as subprocesses
— does not duplicate their logic.

Steps run in order, stopping on any failure:

  Step 1 — Cluster setup
    subprocess: plat_scripts/setup_k8s_platform.py
    Creates Kind cluster, installs Calico CNI, creates namespaces,
    deploys PostgreSQL, applies schema, applies network policies,
    installs Nginx ingress.

  Step 2 — Application deployment
    subprocess: plat_scripts/deploy_platform.py
    Builds and loads Docker images, creates Kubernetes Secrets,
    deploys all 6 microservices, applies network policies, configures ingress.

  Step 3 — ELK stack deployment (inline — not a separate script)
    helm install elasticsearch elastic/elasticsearch \
      --namespace monitoring \
      -f uvote-platform/k8s/logging/elasticsearch-values.yaml \
      --timeout 10m --wait
    Wait for elasticsearch-master-0 to be Running 1/1
    helm install kibana elastic/kibana \
      --namespace monitoring \
      -f uvote-platform/k8s/logging/kibana-values.yaml \
      --timeout 5m --wait
    helm install fluent-bit fluent/fluent-bit \
      --namespace monitoring \
      -f uvote-platform/k8s/logging/fluent-bit-values.yaml \
      --timeout 3m --wait

  Step 4 — Final health check
    kubectl get pods -n uvote-dev
    kubectl get pods -n monitoring
    Print summary confirming all pods are Running.

Requirements:

* Same coloured logging style as existing scripts ([INFO], [SUCCESS],
[WARNING], [ERROR])
* Writes log to logs/boot-platform-<timestamp>.log
* Prints elapsed time at end
* Exit code 0 on full success, 1 on any failure
* --skip-cluster flag skips Step 1 (cluster already exists)
* --skip-elk flag skips Step 3 (ELK already deployed)

----

TASK 3 — Create boot_test_platform.py (test/CI orchestrator):

Create boot_test_platform.py at the project root. Identical to
boot_platform.py plus one additional step.

  Step 5 — MailHog deployment
    subprocess: plat_scripts/deploy_test_platform.py
    Deploys MailHog to uvote-dev and uvote-test, creates smtp-credentials
    Secret, applies MailHog network policies, verifies HTTP API.

MailHog is the ONLY difference between boot_platform.py and
boot_test_platform.py.

Same requirements as boot_platform.py:

* Coloured logging, log file to logs/boot-test-platform-<timestamp>.log
* --skip-cluster and --skip-elk flags
* Exit code 0/1
* Final health check confirms uvote-dev, monitoring, and MailHog pods

----

TASK 4 — Verify .gitignore:

* If .gitignore exists: add logs/*.log if not already present
* If .gitignore does not exist: note it is missing, do not create it

----

CONSTRAINTS:

* Do not modify any existing script's core logic — log file path only
* Do not modify any app.py, test file, or conftest
* Pure stdlib only — no new dependencies
* Both new scripts must be runnable from project root:
  python boot_platform.py
  python boot_test_platform.py

----

* grep -n "log.*\.log" plat_scripts/deploy_platform.py confirms
log path writes to logs/ directory
* grep -n "log.*\.log" plat_scripts/deploy_test_platform.py confirms
log path writes to logs/ directory
* ls -la boot_platform.py boot_test_platform.py logs/.gitkeep
all three files exist
* python -m py_compile boot_platform.py exits 0
* python -m py_compile boot_test_platform.py exits 0
* logs/*.log present in .gitignore
